title: Proration Matrix: On-call Reserve & Deployment Buckets — Q4 2027
summary: Working worksheet to convert qualitative on-call and deployment capacity discussions into a proration matrix that ties budget buckets to deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private) and to headcount phasing. Includes a three-scenario pricing sensitivity run that projects impact to unit economics and required FTE changes to preserve margin targets.

Notes row,Technical assumptions: GPU Reserve = expected min monthly committed GPU spend by bucket. Token Buffer expressed in millions of tokens; used to smooth billing spikes for hosted. Proration rules are a mix of fixed % allocations and trigger-driven pulls from a central contingency. All numbers are rough order of magnitude for planning; finalize after Q4 traffic telemetry.
pricing_sensitivity_scenarios: Scenario: Base (Current pricing + expected demand) — Assumptions: +12% q/q hosted token growth; average token price = $0.00080; effective unit cost (infra+ops) = $0.00035/token. Result: contribution margin ~56%; target: maintain >50% after hiring. Required incremental FTEs: +2 infra eng (H2 hiring) to support automation rollout.

Scenario: Price Compression (-20% list price) — Assumptions: list price cut to $0.00064/token; demand elasticity +18% tokens; infra cost per token reduced 5% via batching/quant; Result: contribution margin ~44% (breach). Actions: hold non-essential hires, reassign 1.0 FTE from observability to cost-ops, accelerate quantization pilot to recoup 6ppt margin. Contingency trigger: margin <48% for two months.

Scenario: Demand Surge (+40% tokens) without price change — Assumptions: token demand +40% q/q from new enterprise uptake; unit infra cost increases 12% due to GPU saturation; Result: contribution margin ~50% (at risk). Actions: activate BurstSpot scaling, negotiate temporary spot capacity, requisition 3-month contractor pool for release engineering, and consider a temporary surcharge on dedicated contracts. Contingency trigger: sustained 30% utilization above baseline for >3 weeks.
headcount_plan_high_level: Ramp notes,Use contractors for Q1 burst work if price compression scenario hits; permanent hires delayed until mid-Q2 if margins recover.
budget_phasing_and_triggers: Allocation runway: Central contingency = $1.2M (unallocated) as of start Q4; recommended holdback 18% to cover worst-case price compression.

Trigger: If contribution margin <50% for 2 consecutive closed months: pause noncritical hiring, move $250k from central contingency to oncall reserve, and run immediate 30-day cost optimization sprint.
Trigger: If token demand growth >25% and cloud spot index < baseline: pre-authorize $400k burst spot budget release for 90 days.

Pricing negotiation lever: For DedicatedPool customers >$75k/mo, aim for 6–8% price uplift for committed multi-region SLA to fund reserved GPUs; modeled uplift increases margin by ~4ppt across enterprise book.
assumptions_and_calc_notes: Key assumptions: average token = 3.4K chars ~ 0.68 USD cents at list; infra cost computed as GPU amortization + power + networking + scheduler overhead + SRE time. We assume quantization reductions of 5–15% on token cost when pilot completes (Q1). On-call comp reserve prorated to active incidents and estimated at $11.6k per full-time on-call slot per month (total comp+overhead). All figures preliminary and require telemetry-backed inputs (per-route token mix, KV cache hit-rate).
open_questions: Should on-call reserve be charged back to product teams by incident count or remain centralized? Pros/cons documented in linked Confluence doc.
What is a defensible surcharge for private deployments to cover networking+KMS+audit overhead without pricing out SMB customers?
Confirm elasticity assumption: do we believe price elasticity > 0.5 on hosted token price? If yes, deeper price experiments needed before any permanent cuts.
